heroHeadline: DR Pledges $20M to GSF; CEP Sets 30,000-Member Election Bar as Saint-Marc Curfew Signals Artibonite Gang Spread
heroSubtitle: On May 5, 2026, the Dominican Republic formally committed $20 million to the UN Gang Suppression Force Trust Fund in a two-year tranche ($10M in 2026, $10M in 2027), bringing total pledged contributions to over $220 million from 13+ states — though only $59 million has been disbursed — as the GSF's 545-person advance contingent (400 Chadian, 75 Guatemalan, 70 Salvadoran) continues joint operations with the Haitian National Police following Kenya's final MSS departure on April 28. The same day, the municipality of Saint-Marc — a strategic Artibonite port city on Route Nationale 1, the main artery between Port-au-Prince and Cap-Haïtien — imposed a nightly curfew banning all vehicle and motorcycle traffic from 8:30 p.m. to 6:00 a.m., citing deteriorating security conditions driven by gang expansion from deeper in the Artibonite Valley following Gran Grif's March–April offensive that killed 16–70 people in Jean-Denis and displaced 13,000+. On May 6, Haiti's Provisional Electoral Council (CEP) announced that political parties must have a minimum of 30,000 registered members to field candidates in the planned August 30, 2026 elections — a requirement that could disqualify most of the 320 CEP-approved parties — as voter registration remains postponed indefinitely pending an unissued electoral decree and 23 communes remain inaccessible due to gang control. On May 7, Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé announced an official diplomatic mission to Rome and the Vatican (May 8–11), while a Haitian ministry simultaneously requested PNH and FAd'H security protection for quarry operations under gang extortion threat — illustrating the continued spread of armed criminality into Haiti's productive sector. Gang control of Port-au-Prince remains contested: PM Fils-Aimé claimed a reduction to approximately 75% on May 1, while UN BINUH's most recent independent estimate stands at approximately 90% as of March 2026. A US Supreme Court ruling on TPS (Noem v. Doe / Trump v. Miot) affecting approximately 350,000 Haitian TPS holders remains pending after April 29 oral arguments; a decision is expected by late June or early July 2026.
